newsitem.title: USA: CME denounces U.S. court decision on forex trading.
newsitem.headline: CME denounces U.S. court decision on forex trading.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) denounced a U.S. appeals court decision exempting all off-exchange foreign currency futures transactions from Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) oversight.
"This ruling is exactly the kind of disaster we feared and have been fighting to prevent," CME chairman Jack Sandner said in a statement.

The U.S. Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled against the CFTC this week in the CFTC's case against Frankwell Bullion Ltd, affirming a 1995 lower court decision that the CFTC could not prosecute Frankwell under the Commodity Exchange Act.

Sandner said this week's ruling reinforces the need for a legislative solution to modify the Treasury amendment to the Commodity Exchange Act and to ensure that off-exchange bucket shops "are put out of business."
"This bucket shop sub-culture, operating virtually free of any regulation, will grow into a national disaster if Congress does not act quickly," Sandner said.
He said the exchange sent letters on Thursday to congressional leaders calling for the reintroduction of strong legislation when Congress reconvenes next year.

"The thoughtful legislation introduced last month in the House by Rep. Thomas Ewing (R-Ill.) addresses this issue appropriately and should be reintroduced in its present form," CME president Bill Brodsky said in a statement. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
